name: Opportunity
summary: A solar-powered rover planned for 90 sols that worked for more than 14 years and found evidence that water once shaped its landing region.
discoveries: Found evidence that liquid water once existed at Meridiani Planum.
Drove more than a marathon distance across the Martian surface.

stories.kids: I was built for a 90-day job and kept going for more than 14 years. I found proof that water once soaked this land. In 2018 a giant dust storm blocked the sunlight I needed, and I went quiet.
stories.explorer: Opportunity landed in January 2004 and explored Meridiani Planum, studying rocks that recorded a wetter Martian past. A planet-wide dust storm in 2018 cut off its solar power. NASA declared the mission complete on February 13, 2019.
stories.scientist: Opportunity operated at Meridiani Planum from 2004 to 2018. Last contact was June 10, 2018, during a planet-encircling dust storm that limited solar power. Total odometry was 45.16 km.

timeline.title: Landing at Meridiani Planum
timeline.text: Opportunity begins a mission planned for 90 sols.

timeline.title: Last contact, in a dust storm
timeline.text: A planet-encircling dust storm blocks the sunlight the solar panels need. Opportunity drove 45.16 km in all.

timeline.title: Mission complete
timeline.text: NASA declares the mission complete on February 13, 2019.

learn.title: Who I am
learn.text: I’m Opportunity, a solar-powered rover. I landed on Meridiani Planum on January 25, 2004, built for a mission of 90 sols.

learn.title: My long life
learn.text: I worked on Mars for more than 14 years and drove 45.16 km, farther than a marathon. I found evidence that water once existed here.

learn.title: The storm
learn.text: In June 2018 a planet-wide dust storm blocked the sunlight my solar panels needed. My last contact was on June 10, 2018.
